title: Cervical Stimulation
description: The cervix has its own distinct nerve supply — including partial innervation via the vagus nerve — and produces a response many people describe as unlike anything else: deep, diffuse, sometimes felt throughout the torso. Most people have never accessed it deliberately.
equipment: Generous water-based or silicone-based lubricant. A curved toy or dildo long enough to reach the posterior fornix (the area around and behind the cervix). A pillow under the hips is useful.
safetyNote: Cervical sensitivity varies across the menstrual cycle — often highest around ovulation, lowest just after menstruation. Start there if uncertain. Use gradual, sustained pressure — not thrusting or impact. Sharp pain means stop and reduce depth. Accidental rough contact can cause cramping; this experience is about steady gentle pressure, not force.

instructions.label: Solo
instructions.content: Lie on your back with a pillow under your hips. Insert a curved toy slowly, directing pressure toward the anterior fornix first — the area just in front of and above the cervix — which is often accessible before the cervix itself and tends to be less sensitive. Apply slow, steady pressure rather than thrusting. When you've located the cervix directly — you'll recognise it as a distinct rounded structure with a different firmness — apply gentle, sustained pressure against it. Hold rather than move. The response, if it arrives, is often felt broadly rather than locally: a diffuse, deep sensation sometimes described as spreading through the abdomen or lower torso. Stay with sustained pressure and note what builds.

instructions.label: With a partner
instructions.content: Position matters more here than in most penetrative experiences. The receiver experiments with what allows the deepest comfortable access: on their back with hips elevated, on all fours, or a variation specific to their anatomy. Once depth is reached, the giver holds steady rather than thrusting — this is about sustained contact, not movement. The receiver communicates moment to moment: what registers as sensation, what tips toward discomfort, when to hold and when to adjust. Combining gentle cervical pressure with external stimulation produces, for many people, a response categorically different from either alone.

As giver: does the slower, more positionally precise quality of this produce a different kind of attention than other forms of penetration?
why: The cervix is partially innervated by the vagus nerve — a pathway that bypasses the spinal cord and connects directly to the brain. This is why it can produce sensation in people with certain spinal injuries who have no other pelvic sensation, and for everyone else it means the response often has a different character from stimulation delivered through standard pelvic pathways. Many people describe it as deeper and more diffuse than clitoral or G-spot stimulation — something felt throughout the lower body rather than at a precise point. Most people have encountered the cervix accidentally during deep penetration, usually as an uncomfortable bump; deliberate, gentle sustained contact is categorically different from accidental impact, and produces a response most people have never actually tested.
